label: thm:pacf_controllable
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:pacf_controllable}
For $N\geqslant 7$,\footnote{It is feasible to fully characterize the $N\leqslant 6$ case. It is deliberately neglected because the analysis is tedious and has limited practical value.} the \ac{islr} is type-based controllable, if and only if the modulation basis $ 
  \ifcat\noexpandU\relax\bm{\csname var\expandafter\@gobble\stringU\endcsname}\else\bm{U}\fi
$ satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{islr_controllable_u}
 
  \ifcat\noexpandU\relax\bm{\csname var\expandafter\@gobble\stringU\endcsname}\else\bm{U}\fi
= 
  \ifcat\noexpandF\relax\bm{\csname var\expandafter\@gobble\stringF\endcsname}\else\bm{F}\fi
_N^{\rm H} 
  \ifcat\noexpandM\relax\bm{\csname var\expandafter\@gobble\stringM\endcsname}\else\bm{M}\fi
 
  \ifcat\noexpandC\relax\bm{\csname var\expandafter\@gobble\stringC\endcsname}\else\bm{C}\fi
_{\alpha,\beta},
\end{equation}
where $ 
  \ifcat\noexpandM\relax\bm{\csname var\expandafter\@gobble\stringM\endcsname}\else\bm{M}\fi
\in\mathsf{Mon}(N)$, $\alpha,\beta\in[0,2\pi)$, and $ 
  \ifcat\noexpandC\relax\bm{\csname var\expandafter\@gobble\stringC\endcsname}\else\bm{C}\fi
_{\alpha,\beta}$ is defined by
\begin{equation}
 
  \ifcat\noexpandC\relax\bm{\csname var\expandafter\@gobble\stringC\endcsname}\else\bm{C}\fi
_{\alpha,\beta}=\frac{e^{j\alpha}}{N}\bm{1}\bm{1}^{\rm T}+e^{j\beta}( 
  \ifcat\noexpandI\relax\bm{\csname var\expandafter\@gobble\stringI\endcsname}\else\bm{I}\fi
-\bm{1}\bm{1}^{\rm T}).
\end{equation}
\begin{IEEEproof}
Please refer to Appendix \ref{ssec:proof_pacf_controllable}.
\end{IEEEproof}

title: Remark
body_md: Note that the entire $\widetilde{c}_m[\nu]$ sequence is a length-$N$ \ac{pacf}, and hence can be obtained by a single \ac{fft} and its inverse. Therefore, the overall complexity of the algorithm is on the order of $O(MN\log N)$. From the communication perspective, in order to inform the communication receiver with the circular shifts, $\lceil\log_2 N\rceil$ additional bits would have to be consumed for each \ac{ofdm} symbol.

In this way, \ac{qam} are made compatible with \ac{pas}.

label: lem:commutation
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:commutation}
If a unitary matrix $ 
  \ifcat\noexpandC\relax\bm{\csname var\expandafter\@gobble\stringC\endcsname}\else\bm{C}\fi
$ commutes with all permutation matrices in $\mathscr{S}_N$, we have
\begin{equation}\label{c_ab}
 
  \ifcat\noexpandC\relax\bm{\csname var\expandafter\@gobble\stringC\endcsname}\else\bm{C}\fi
= 
  \ifcat\noexpandC\relax\bm{\csname var\expandafter\@gobble\stringC\endcsname}\else\bm{C}\fi
_{\alpha,\beta}:=e^{j\beta} 
  \ifcat\noexpandI\relax\bm{\csname var\expandafter\@gobble\stringI\endcsname}\else\bm{I}\fi
+\frac{1}{N}(e^{j\alpha}-e^{j\beta})\bm{1}\bm{1}^{\rm T}.
\end{equation}
\begin{IEEEproof}
Using the classical orbital basis result on the centralizer algebra of permutation representations \cite[Sec.~2.2]{cameron_permgroup}, we obtain
\begin{equation}
 
  \ifcat\noexpandC\relax\bm{\csname var\expandafter\@gobble\stringC\endcsname}\else\bm{C}\fi
\in{\rm span}\{ 
  \ifcat\noexpandI\relax\bm{\csname var\expandafter\@gobble\stringI\endcsname}\else\bm{I}\fi
,\bm{1}\bm{1}^{\rm T}\}.
\end{equation}
Using the unitarity of $ 
  \ifcat\noexpandC\relax\bm{\csname var\expandafter\@gobble\stringC\endcsname}\else\bm{C}\fi
$, it follows that the eigenvalues on ${\rm span}(\bm{1})$ and its orthogonal complement are both unimodular, thus leading to \eqref{c_ab}.
\end{IEEEproof}
Using Lemma \ref{lem:commutation}, we finally obtain
\begin{equation}
 
  \ifcat\noexpandV\relax\bm{\csname var\expandafter\@gobble\stringV\endcsname}\else\bm{V}\fi
= 
  \ifcat\noexpandD\relax\bm{\csname var\expandafter\@gobble\stringD\endcsname}\else\bm{D}\fi
 
  \ifcat\noexpand\Xi\relax\bm{\csname var\expandafter\@gobble\string\Xi\endcsname}\else\bm{\Xi}\fi
 
  \ifcat\noexpandC\relax\bm{\csname var\expandafter\@gobble\stringC\endcsname}\else\bm{C}\fi
_{\alpha,\beta}^{\rm H}= 
  \ifcat\noexpandD\relax\bm{\csname var\expandafter\@gobble\stringD\endcsname}\else\bm{D}\fi
 
  \ifcat\noexpand\Xi\relax\bm{\csname var\expandafter\@gobble\string\Xi\endcsname}\else\bm{\Xi}\fi
 
  \ifcat\noexpandC\relax\bm{\csname var\expandafter\@gobble\stringC\endcsname}\else\bm{C}\fi
_{-\alpha,-\beta},
\end{equation}
where $ 
  \ifcat\noexpandD\relax\bm{\csname var\expandafter\@gobble\stringD\endcsname}\else\bm{D}\fi
 
  \ifcat\noexpand\Xi\relax\bm{\csname var\expandafter\@gobble\string\Xi\endcsname}\else\bm{\Xi}\fi
\in\mathsf{Mon}(N)$.

title: Proof
body_md: The sufficiency is straightforward since the sidelobes of a sequence having a single non-zero entry are obviously all zero. Conversely, assume by contradiction that $\bm{s}$ has at least two non-zero entries, let $i<j$ be the smallest and the largest non-zero indices. We see that for $k=j-i$, the autocorrelation $r_k=\sum_{n} s_n^*s_{n+k}$ is non-zero since the product $s_n^*s_{n+k}$ is only non-zero when $n=i$. This implies that $A_{\rm a}(\bm{s})>0$, and hence the original assumption is false. This completes the proof.
